newsitem.title: UK: Jazzman Ronnie Scott's death still a mystery.
newsitem.headline: Jazzman Ronnie Scott's death still a mystery.

text.p: The death of British saxophonist Ronnie Scott, whose London club brought many of the world's top jazz musicians to England, remains a mystery, an inquest heard on Tuesday.
Scott collapsed and died at his London home on December 23 at the age of 69.
A post-mortem failed to establish the cause of death, although Scott's business partner Peter King said his friend was depressed and had attempted suicide in the past.
"Ronnie was depressed for some time and had attempted to take his own life on more than one occasion in 1966," King said in a statement read to a London coroner's court.
"He had had problems with his teeth and this had made it difficult for him to play his instruments."
The inquest was adjourned to enable further tests to be made. Police were investigating a theory that Scott took his life after becoming depressed about his imminent 70th birthday.
Scott founded his club in London's Soho district in 1959, and made a name for himself with the irreverent comic monologues he used to introduce performers.
